method: bycatch records from three tiger-survey camera-trap deployments; photographic records of sun bears separated by a minimum interval (value missing from the text read) used to plot the activity pattern by kernel density estimation
conditions: Wild sun bears, Bukit Barisan Selatan National Park, Sumatra, Indonesia; three camera-trap surveys: Intensive Protection Zone May-Nov 2015 (8,831 trap-days, 63 locations, 261 photographs, 115 independent events), North Apr-Oct 2018 (6,887 trap-days, 61 locations, 431 photographs, 65 independent events), Intensive Protection Zone May-Nov 2019 (9,195 trap-days, 65 locations, 1,882 photographs, 191 independent events) (Table 1); the paper does not state how many photographs or events entered the activity analysis. Results: most photographs were recorded during the day, followed by night; activity was bimodal and similar near modified habitat and in forest interior.

method: camera traps at 238 sites; independent events; daily activity pattern from event times
conditions: Wild Williamson's mouse deer, three protected areas in Mengla County, Yunnan, China; 238 camera-trap sites, January 2017 to January 2021, 105,087 camera-trap days (78 to 1,118 days per site); 921 independent events of this species at 32 sites (17,561 events across the five ungulate species). Peaks at 9:00 and 18:00 and a trough at 13:00. The same section reports other ungulates with varied degrees of nocturnal activity and sambar mainly active at night; these are not part of this record.
